Metric Spaces

This scene axiomatizes distance. Compare how the shape of a ball changes when the metric changes.

A metric obeys only three rules. Distances are never negative. The distance is the same both ways. A detour is never shorter than the direct way. Same rules, different measurement: balls of equal radius take different shapes.

For example, change how a 📏 ruler measures between two points. Measure straight, and you get a disk. Measure along grid lines only, and you get a diamond. Same radius, different reach.

Prove every subset of a discrete metric space is open.

B(x,1/2)={x}B(x, 1/2) = \{x\}B(x,1/2)={x}
Show proof

  1. Let AAA be any subset of a discrete metric space. If A=∅A = \emptysetA=∅, then AAA is open vacuously — there is no point of AAA at which openness could fail.

Prove a convergent sequence in a discrete metric space is eventually constant.

d(xn,x)<1/2  ⟹  xn=xd(x_n, x) < 1/2 \implies x_n = xd(xn​,x)<1/2⟹xn​=x
